title: HfO2/MgF2 29-layer UV bandpass with relaxed edge bounds and reduced curvature regularization
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack with asymmetric thickness tuning can produce a transmission peak in 255-280 nm while maintaining suppression in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands, and broader thickness perturbation ranges will escape the rigid alternating pattern observed in prior rounds.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film physics: alternating high/low index layers create distributed Bragg reflectors; transmission bands appear at wavelengths where the optical thickness condition is violated or at intentional defect layers. MgF2 has low absorption in deep UV; HfO2 provides high index contrast. Breaking quarter-wave symmetry can shift the passband.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | SiO2 substrate (29 film layers total)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers with bounds relaxed to ±2.0 nm from initial quarter-wave values
curvature regularization weight reduced from 0.15 to 0.08
thickness reinitialization with broader uniform perturbation to break alternating pattern
soft_objectives: maintain physical validity of all candidates
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 29 (under 30-layer limit)
HfO2 and MgF2 are conventional e-beam or thermal evaporable dielectrics
individual layer thicknesses should remain in depositable range 30-200 nm
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stack reflectance bandwidth scales with index ratio nH/nL
Recalled: MgF2 remains transparent down to ~120 nm, suitable for 255-280 nm UV
Recalled: HfO2 has high index (~2.0-2.4 in UV) and low extinction in solar-blind region
Recalled: Breaking periodicity in layer thicknesses can create transmission defects in Bragg mirrors
Recalled: Edge layers have disproportionate effect on impedance matching and passband shape
expected_advantages: Relaxed edge bounds allow larger impedance-matching adjustments at air and substrate interfaces
Reduced curvature regularization permits more aggressive thickness variation between adjacent layers
Broader perturbation ranges should escape local minima from rigid alternating patterns
HfO2/MgF2 pair offers sufficient index contrast for UV bandpass without metal absorption losses
known_risks: I am uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal versus fewer layers; this was chosen to stay under 30-layer limit while maximizing design freedom
I recall HfO2 absorption increases below 250 nm but am uncertain of exact extinction coefficient at 255 nm; measured dataset will resolve this
The exact quarter-wave thickness at 265 nm (center of passband) depends on refractive indices I have not looked up; initial guesses may be off by 10-20%
Curvature regularization weight reduction from 0.15 to 0.08 is a heuristic choice; optimal value is unknown without literature
I am uncertain whether MgF2 stress or adhesion issues would affect 29-layer deposition; this route assumes ideal layers
execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer planar multilayer thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2 (29 film layers). Optimize all 29 layer thicknesses simultaneously. Initial thicknesses: quarter-wave at 265 nm center wavelength using measured n values from hfo2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) datasets. Thickness bounds: ±2.0 nm relaxation from initial quarter-wave values for edge layers (layers 1, 2, 28, 29), ±1.5 nm for interior layers. Curvature regularization weight: 0.08. Reinitialize thickness parameters with uniform perturbation range ±5 nm to break alternating patterns. Spectral targets: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Use gradient_thickness optimizer. Total layers fixed at 29.
revision_reason: Continuation of control route with relaxed edge layer bounds (±1.0 nm to ±2.0 nm), reduced curvature regularization (0.15 to 0.08), and broader thickness perturbation ranges to escape rigid alternating pattern observed in prior rounds per feedback directives.
